"""Shared pytest setup for the notes storage tests.

* Puts the project root on ``sys.path`` so ``import notes`` works no matter how
  pytest is launched (``pytest tests/...`` from a console script does not add
  the root directory by default).
* Provides an autouse guard that fails any test which reads or writes the real
  ``./notes.json`` in the project root.  Tests must use ``tmp_path`` instead.

Standard library plus pytest only.
"""

import os
import pathlib
import sys

import pytest

import notes

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if ROOT not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def guard_real_notes_file():
    """Fail if a test touches the project-root ``notes.json``.

    An absolute path is captured before the test runs, so a test that
    ``monkeypatch.chdir``s into ``tmp_path`` is still checked against the real
    project directory.
    """
    real = pathlib.Path(ROOT) / notes.DEFAULT_PATH
    before = real.read_bytes() if real.is_file() else None

    yield

    after = real.read_bytes() if real.is_file() else None
    assert after == before, (
        "test touched the project-root notes.json; pass an isolated "
        "tmp_path (or chdir into tmp_path) instead"
    )

        metavar="{add,list,delete}",
        required=True,
    )

    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "add",
        parents=[common],
        help="Add a note",
        description="Add a note to the store.",
    )
    add_parser.add_argument(
        "text",
        nargs="+",
        metavar="text",
        help="text of the note (words are joined with single spaces)",
    )

    subparsers.add_parser(
        "list",
        parents=[common],
        help="List notes",
        description="List all notes, numbered from 1.",
    )

    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "delete",
        parents=[common],
        help="Delete a note by its number",
        description="Delete the note with the given 1-based number.",
    )
    delete_parser.add_argument(
        "number",
        type=int,
        metavar="number",
        help="1-based number of the note to delete (see `list`)",
    )

    return parser


def _resolve_file(args):
    """Return the notes file path from *args* (SUPPRESSed defaults included)."""
    path = getattr(args, "file", None)
    return path if path else DEFAULT_FILE


def _format_line(number, note):
    text = note.get("text", "")
    return "%d. %s" % (number, text)


def _run(args):
    """Execute the parsed *args*; return the exit status (0 or 1)."""
    path = _resolve_file(args)

    try:

            text = " ".join(args.text)

            print("Added note: %s" % note.get("text", text))

        elif args.command == "list":
            stored = notes.list_notes(path=path)
            if not stored:
                print(EMPTY_MESSAGE)
            else:
                for number, note in enumerate(stored, start=1):
                    print(_format_line(number, note))

        elif args.command == "delete":
            removed = notes.delete_note(args.number, path=path)
            print("Deleted note %d: %s" % (args.number, removed.get("text", "")))

        else:  # pragma: no cover - argparse rejects unknown commands first

            return 1

    except ValueError as exc:

        print("error: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except OSError as exc:

        return 1

    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    """Run the CLI with *argv* (defaults to ``sys.argv[1:]``).

    Returns the process exit status.  When the module is executed as a script
    the status is raised as ``SystemExit`` so that the shell sees it.
    """
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    status = _run(args)

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        raise SystemExit(status)
    return status

import os
from datetime import datetime

            % (path, type(data).__name__)
        )

    notes = []
    for entry in data:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                "notes file %r must contain JSON objects, found %s"
                % (path, type(entry).__name__)
            )
        notes.append(entry)
    return notes


def _save(path, notes):
    """Write *notes* to *path* as a JSON array, creating directories as needed."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    if directory:
        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(notes, fh, indent=2)
        fh.write("\n")


def add_note(text, path=DEFAULT_PATH):
    """Append a note with *text* to the store and return the stored dict."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError("text must be a str, got %s" % type(text).__name__)

    notes = _load(path)
    note = {"text": text, "created": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    notes.append(note)
    _save(path, notes)
    return dict(note)


def list_notes(path=DEFAULT_PATH):
    """Return all notes as a list of dicts; [] when the file does not exist."""
    return [dict(note) for note in _load(path)]


def delete_note(index, path=DEFAULT_PATH):
    """Delete the 1-based note at *index* and return the removed dict.

    Raises ValueError for non-positive or out-of-range indexes (including
    when the file does not exist, since then nothing is in range).
    """
    if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
        raise TypeError("index must be an int, got %s" % type(index).__name__)

    notes = _load(path)
    if index < 1 or index > len(notes):
        raise ValueError(
            "index %d is out of range (file holds %d note(s))" % (index, len(notes))
        )

    removed = notes.pop(index - 1)
    _save(path, notes)
    return dict(removed)

"""Integration tests for the ``cli.py`` command line front-end.

Every test is hermetic:

* the notes file always lives inside ``tmp_path`` and is passed with
  ``--file``, so the repository's own ``notes.json`` is never read or written
  (``conftest.py`` also asserts that);
* the subprocess helper runs with ``cwd=tmp_path`` and ``PYTHONPATH`` pointing
  at the project root, so ``python cli.py`` is exercised exactly like a user
  would run it, just somewhere harmless.

Both driving styles are covered: in process via ``cli.main([...])`` and out of
process via :func:`subprocess.run`.

Standard library plus pytest only.
"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)

if ROOT not in sys.path:  # allow `pytest tests/test_cli.py` from anywhere
    sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

import cli  # noqa: E402  (import after the sys.path fix-up)
import notes  # noqa: E402

SCRIPT = os.path.join(ROOT, "cli.py")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def read_json(path):
    """Return the parsed contents of the notes file at *path*."""
    with open(str(path), "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def texts(entries):
    return [entry["text"] for entry in entries]


def run_script(*args, cwd):
    """Run ``python cli.py <args>`` in its own process, isolated in *cwd*."""
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = ROOT + (os.pathsep + env["PYTHONPATH"] if env.get("PYTHONPATH") else "")
    env.pop("PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE", None)
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, SCRIPT] + [str(arg) for arg in args],
        cwd=str(cwd),
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )


@pytest.fixture
def notes_file(tmp_path):
    """An absolute, not-yet-created notes file path inside ``tmp_path``."""
    return tmp_path / "data" / "notes.json"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# in-process: cli.main([...])
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_main_add_returns_zero_writes_file_and_prints(notes_file, capsys):
    status = cli.main(["add", "buy milk", "--file", str(notes_file)])

    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert status == 0
    assert captured.err == ""
    assert "buy milk" in captured.out
    assert texts(read_json(notes_file)) == ["buy milk"]


def test_main_add_then_list_shows_the_note_in_order(notes_file, capsys):
    """A note added via the CLI is visible in the very next list output."""
    assert cli.main(["add", "first note", "--file", str(notes_file)]) == 0
    assert cli.main(["add", "second note", "--file", str(notes_file)]) == 0
    add_output = capsys.readouterr().out

    assert cli.main(["list", "--file", str(notes_file)]) == 0
    list_output = capsys.readouterr().out

    assert "first note" in add_output and "second note" in add_output
    assert list_output.splitlines() == ["1. first note", "2. second note"]


def test_main_add_joins_words_with_spaces(notes_file, capsys):
    assert cli.main(["add", "two", "words", "--file", str(notes_file)]) == 0
    capsys.readouterr()
    assert texts(read_json(notes_file)) == ["two words"]

    notes.add_note("second", path=str(notes_file))
